The comment governs only how values are reported on the DMR (geometric mean of weekly values) while numeric limits may still use a different statistic (e.g., 30-day average) for enforcement comparison.
The geometric-mean comment is TDS-specific permit language propagated at limit-set level to unrelated parameters; it does not change comparison semantics for non-TDS limits.
Structured sources do not establish how monthly DMR values relate to weekly geometric means or which aggregation window applies for limit comparison.

grounding.establishes: Footnote *6 ties TDS discharge reporting at Outfall 001 to reporting the geometric mean of weekly values; a separate net-increase row carries a numeric 497 mg/L limit.
Footnote *8 defines net TDS as a derived quantity (discharge minus flow-weighted influent average), not a single raw sample.
The enforceable TDS net incremental increase limit is described as a 30-day average (497 mg/L, later revised to 449 mg/L), distinct from geometric-mean weekly discharge reporting language.
Elsewhere in the permit package, geometric-mean limits are stated with an explicit monthly window (E. coli), showing geometric mean is used with different aggregation windows in different contexts.
A BOD (PARAMETER_CODE 00310) limit row carries DMR comment text that explicitly names TDS and geometric-mean weekly reporting while STATISTICAL_BASE_TYPE_CODE is AVG.
The TDS limit row (PARAMETER_CODE 70295) carries the same geometric-mean comment, STATISTICAL_BASE_TYPE_CODE AVG, and numeric limit 497.
A monthly BOD measurement is stored as a single numeric value with AVG statistical base despite the paired limit row's geometric-mean comment.
A monthly TDS measurement is stored as a single numeric value (269) paired against limit 497 with AVG statistical base; no weekly sub-sample or geometric-mean field is present.

judgment.remaining_uncertainty: Workspace sources establish that (a) TDS discharge reporting language calls for geometric mean of weekly values, (b) TDS net-increase enforcement is described as a 30-day average, and (c) the same geometric-mean DMR comment propagates to non-TDS parameters within a limit set. They do not establish how an individual monthly monitoring-period DMR value should be compared to a numeric limit when the geometric-mean comment is present: whether the monthly value is already a pre-aggregated geometric mean, whether comparison must use weekly sub-period aggregation, or whether the comment governs reporting only while a different statistic governs enforcement comparison. All 40 structured rows encode AVG/MAX/MIN bases only; weekly sub-period measurements are absent from dmr_measurements.csv; and no codebook maps structured fields to geometric mean.

children.relation_contract: TDS aggregated weekly geometric-mean reporting is not an ordinary single-period numeric comparison

refinement.why_necessary: All 40 occurrences share one identical DMR_COMMENT_TEXT that explicitly names TDS at Outfall 001, but structured data attaches it to 10 parameters (BOD, pH, TSS, cyanide, flow, chlorine, E. coli, TDS, percent removals). Permit footnote *6 authoritatively applies only to TDS discharge reporting. TDS net-increase limits use 30-day average enforcement language in the statement of basis, while footnote *6 requires geometric mean of weekly values — a materially different question than whether BOD monthly values should skip ordinary comparison because of a TDS comment copied at limit-set level.
